NexaCore Security Policy

Version 5.3 | Enterprise Security Baseline

Owner: Security Engineering    Effective: 01 Aug 2026    Review: 31 Jul 2027

1. Security Governance and Scope

This policy establishes the security baseline for NexaCore systems, employees, contractors, applications and information
assets. The dataset is synthetic private-company data created for RAG evaluation and is not sourced from a real organization.

1.1 Security objectives

• Protect confidentiality of company and customer information.

• Preserve integrity of production systems and business records.

• Maintain availability of critical services within approved recovery targets.

• Detect and respond to security events using documented ownership and escalation.

• Apply least privilege and measurable access controls.

1.2 Information classification

| Classification   | Examples                                       | Default handling                           |
|:-----------------|:-----------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Public           | Approved marketing material                    | External distribution permitted            |
| Internal         | Policies, engineering docs                     | Company access                             |
| Confidential     | Contracts, source code, financial records      | Need-to-know                               |
| Restricted       | Credentials, security findings, regulated data | Explicit authorization + enhanced controls |

1.3 Security ownership

The CISO delegate owns policy governance. Security Engineering operates preventive and detective controls. System owners
remain accountable for security of the systems they operate.

2. Identity, Authentication and Access

2.1 Identity baseline

• Corporate identity is required for workforce access to managed systems.

• Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for production, administrative and remote access.

• Shared human accounts are prohibited except approved break-glass mechanisms.

• Service accounts must have an owner, documented purpose and credential rotation plan.

• Access must be removed or changed when employment or role status changes.

2.2 Authentication controls

| Control                          | Requirement                                         |
|:---------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------|
| MFA                              | Required for privileged and remote access           |
| Password length                  | Minimum 14 characters where passwords are supported |
| Session timeout                  | 15 min inactivity for privileged consoles           |
| Privileged re-authentication     | Every 12 hours or after risk event                  |
| Failed authentication monitoring | 5 failures / 15 min triggers detection              |

2.3 Joiner / mover / leaver

Standard access changes should be completed within 4 business hours of an approved HR event. Terminated users with
immediate security concern require access revocation as soon as the event is received.

3. Application and Infrastructure Security

3.1 Secure development

• Security requirements are reviewed for internet-facing and sensitive applications before production launch.

• Dependencies are scanned continuously; confirmed critical exposure is targeted for remediation within 24 hours.

• Secrets must be retrieved from approved secret management and must not be committed to source control.

• Production debug modes are prohibited.

• Security-sensitive actions require audit logging.

3.2 Infrastructure controls

| Area                  | Minimum baseline                                 |
|:----------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| Network               | Segment public ingress, workloads and data paths |
| Storage               | Encryption at rest where supported               |
| Transport             | TLS for sensitive data in transit                |
| Backups               | Encrypted + access controlled                    |
| Administrative access | Privileged identity + MFA + logging              |
| Endpoint              | Managed device for privileged operations         |

3.3 Vulnerability severity

Reference remediation targets: Critical ≤24 hours, High ≤7 calendar days, Medium ≤30 calendar days, Low ≤90 calendar days.
Active exploitation can trigger emergency treatment regardless of severity label.

4. Data Protection and Monitoring

4.1 Data handling

• Restricted information may only be stored in approved systems.

• Customer data must not be copied to personal devices or unapproved collaboration tools.

• Production data used for development must be masked, minimized or replaced with synthetic data.

• Exports containing Confidential or Restricted information require approved destination and access controls.

• Data retention follows the corporate record schedule and applicable contractual requirements.

4.2 Logging requirements

| Event                         | Minimum logging                                  |
|:------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| Authentication                | User/service, timestamp, result, source context  |
| Privilege change              | Actor, target, old/new privilege, timestamp      |
| Security configuration change | Actor, object, change and result                 |
| Sensitive data access         | Identity, resource and timestamp where supported |
| Incident action               | Responder, action, time and ticket/reference     |

4.3 Monitoring

Security monitoring prioritizes authentication anomalies, privilege escalation, suspicious network behavior, malware indicators,
data-exfiltration signals and unusual administrative activity.

5. Third-Party, Endpoint and Physical Controls

5.1 Third-party security

• Vendors handling Confidential or Restricted data require security due diligence before onboarding.

• Security review considers data types, access scope, incident notification, retention and subcontractors.

• Vendor access should be time-bounded where practical.

• Material security findings require an owner and remediation plan.

5.2 Endpoint baseline

| Control                 | Baseline                                                                 |
|:------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Disk encryption         | Required on managed laptops                                              |
| Screen lock             | ≤10 minutes inactivity                                                   |
| OS updates              | Critical security updates within 14 days; emergency faster when directed |
| EDR/endpoint protection | Required for managed corporate endpoints                                 |
| Local administrator     | Restricted; exception-based                                              |

5.3 Physical security

Restricted work areas, server infrastructure and security operations spaces require controlled entry. Visitors must be
accompanied or registered according to site procedure.

6.2 Exceptions

Exceptions require business justification, risk statement, compensating control, owner, approver and expiry date. Security
exceptions normally expire after 90 days unless renewed.

6.3 Governance

• Weekly vulnerability triage.

• Monthly security operations review.

• Quarterly privileged-access certification.

• Quarterly vendor-risk review for high-risk suppliers.

• Annual policy review and security-awareness refresh.

units.content: Vendor management begins at supplier identification and continues through onboarding, contracting, performance monitoring, risk review, renewal and offboarding.

units.content:

Business continuity evidence
References for material strategic suppliers

units.title: 2.3 Risk bands
units.content: Scores below 30 are Low, 30–59 Medium, 60–79 High and 80–100 Critical. A high or critical rating requires a documented mitigation plan before production dependency.

units.title: 3.1 Contract controls
units.content:
Executed agreement must be stored in the approved contract repository.
Material amendments require review of pricing, scope, security and service levels.
Auto-renewal dates should be tracked at least 90 days in advance.
Termination rights and notice periods must be recorded in the vendor record.

units.title: 3.3 Service credits
units.content: Contractual service credits are tracked by Procurement and Finance. Acceptance of a service credit does not automatically waive other contractual remedies.

units.title: 4.2 Score interpretation
units.content: Scores ≥90 are Preferred, 80–89 Healthy, 70–79 Watch and <70 Corrective Action Required.

units.title: 4.3 Corrective action
units.content:
Document issue and evidence.
Agree corrective action and due date.
Assign supplier and internal owners.
Track weekly for critical issues.
Escalate unresolved high-risk issues to Procurement Head.
Consider alternate supplier if remediation fails.

units.title: 5.1 Renewal timeline
units.content:
120 days before expiry: confirm business need and spend.
90 days: performance and risk review.
60 days: commercial negotiation / alternatives.
30 days: final approval and contract execution.
Post-renewal: update vendor record and repository.

units.title: 5.2 Offboarding checklist
units.content:
Revoke system access.
Recover company assets where applicable.
Confirm data return/deletion obligations.
Stop purchase orders.
Close open invoices.
Archive contract and performance record.
Document termination reason.

units.title: 5.3 Exit risk
units.content: Critical vendors require a documented exit plan covering replacement options, data portability, transition period, key dependencies and estimated switching cost.

units.title: 6.1 Ownership rules
units.content: Every active vendor must have an internal business owner. Vendors without an owner are placed on the remediation queue and may be suspended from new commitments.

units.title: 1. Discounting Principles
units.content: Discounts are commercial tools, not default pricing. Sales must establish business justification and protect minimum economics before requesting a concession.

units.title: 1.2 Prohibited behavior
units.content:
Splitting an order to avoid a discount threshold.
Backdating an approval.
Describing a discount as a temporary exception when it is intended as recurring pricing.
Offering unapproved free services or implementation credits.
Using a personal promise to compensate for a commercial concession.

units.title: 2.1 Acceptable justification
units.content:
Multi-year commitment
Material expansion volume
Competitive displacement
Strategic reference account
Pre-approved segment promotion
Contract consolidation

units.title: 2.3 Margin protection
units.content: Discount approval does not override minimum gross-margin requirements. Finance may reject a discount even when the approval level is otherwise satisfied if the proposed economics fall below the product or deal floor.

units.title: 3.2 Renewal rules
units.content:
Renewal discounts must be evaluated against current contract value, usage and expansion potential.
A renewal discount cannot be assumed from the prior year's concession.
Expansion and renewal discounts should be separated in the commercial proposal.
Credits for service issues require Customer Success and Finance validation.

units.title: 3.3 Price protection
units.content: Price-protection clauses extending beyond 12 months require Finance review because they affect future price realization and forecast assumptions.

units.title: 4.2 Valuation
units.content: Non-cash concessions must be recorded at their estimated internal cost or list value, whichever is required by Finance's commercial model. Sales must not hide concession value by presenting it as an unrelated free item.

units.title: 4.3 Free pilots
units.content: A standard proof-of-value should not exceed 30 calendar days without documented extension approval. Any production use during a free period must have explicit data, security and support ownership.

units.title: 5.1 Workflow
units.content:
Create commercial request in CRM.
Attach pricing proposal and justification.
Manager reviews economics and customer context.
Finance reviews margin where required.
Authorized approver accepts/rejects.
Revenue Operations records final approved discount before quote issuance.

units.title: 5.3 Audit controls
units.content: Revenue Operations samples approved discounts monthly. Any discount without an approval record is treated as an exception and may be excluded from commissionable bookings until resolved.

units.title: 6.2 Control objective
units.content:
The FY27 objective is to keep average discount below 7.5% while preserving strategic win rates. Revenue Operations should distinguish pricing pressure from avoidable discounting caused by weak qualification or late commercial planning.
